overview: Implementation study in one veterinary practice: facilitated biosecurity planning visits for consenting client dairy herds, with observed adoption of five core measures at baseline and six months and a record of how visits were delivered.
population: Client dairy herds of the practice whose farmers give written agreement; herds under a disease-control restriction at baseline are excluded until it is lifted.
exposure: One facilitated planning visit by the herd's own vet (about two hours), agreeing three farm-specific priorities from five core measures (isolation of purchased cattle, visitor controls, footbath use, vehicle hygiene, boundary contact), with a follow-up call at six weeks.
procedures: At baseline a second vet observes the five measures during an unannounced visit. The herd's vet then holds the planning visit using a short structured guide and records the priorities agreed. The follow-up call checks progress. At six months the observing vet repeats the unannounced visit. Delivery is recorded with a fidelity checklist; farmers rate acceptability on a five-point scale.

outcomes.name: Observed core measures in place
outcomes.measure: Number of five core measures observed in place at the unannounced visit
outcomes.why: Adoption on the farm is what protects the herd, and observation avoids self-report bias.

outcomes.name: Delivery as planned
outcomes.measure: Proportion of planning visits and follow-up calls completed with every checklist element
outcomes.why: Separates a strategy that failed from one that was not delivered.

outcomes.name: Reach
outcomes.measure: Proportion of invited herds that agree to take part, by herd size and tenure
outcomes.why: Shows which farms the approach reaches.

outcomes.name: Vet time per herd
outcomes.measure: Minutes of vet time per herd including travel
outcomes.why: The practice can only sustain what fits its vets' time.

feasibility: Two vets at one half-day a week each give about 50 half-days over six months, enough for about 20 herds at two observation visits and one planning visit each.
biasMitigation: Unannounced observation by a vet who did not deliver the planning visit
Fixed list of five measures defined before baseline
Reach reported by herd size and tenure

biasFlags.label: Volunteer herds
biasFlags.note: Farms that agree may be keener; reach is reported.

biasFlags.label: Seasonal change
biasFlags.note: Spring turnout changes cattle movements; timing is fixed for all herds.

flags: Two process and one balancing measure
parsimony.simplestPath: One visit type, one observed outcome, two observation points.

theoreticalFramework: RE-AIM to organise reach, adoption, implementation fidelity and maintenance; it earns its place because the question is delivery.
summary: Implementation study with observed adoption as the primary outcome and fidelity, reach and vet time recorded.
